name: Skateboarding and scooter lessons
summary: How expats book skateboard and kick-scooter lessons in Singapore for kids and beginners — park rules, protective gear, and heat/rain scheduling realities.
body:
Skate and scoot coaching uses ActiveSG parks, condo voids (where allowed), and private indoor spaces. Parents want fall-safety habits before unsupervised park sessions; adults want commute-scooter confidence beyond footpath chaos.

## Formats
- Kids’ group fundamentals (stance, braking, falling safe)
- Private coaching for tricks or commute skills
- Holiday camps at skate parks
- Adaptive or confidence-first sessions for anxious beginners

Helmets and wrist guards are non-negotiable for learners despite “it feels hot” protests.

## Rules and etiquette
Park sessions have peak-hour crowding and unwritten lane etiquette. Condos may ban scooters in corridors — check before practising at home. Public-path PMD rules are separate from skatepark play; coaches should not teach illegal footpath speeds as normal.

## How to choose
Watch coach-to-kid ratios and whether gear is provided or BYO. Prefer programmes with rain plans and sunscreen breaks. Ask about progression beyond standing push-offs before buying premium boards.

## Practical tip
Book early-morning or evening classes; midday concrete is brutal. Bring water and shoes with grip — school shoes with smooth soles waste the lesson.
